title: Ten Out of Ten in Pencil  (铅笔写下的十分满分)

segments.t: 回到咖啡柜台前，泰莎切开了仍然温热的三号烤模蛋糕，表面闪烁着金黄蜂蜜、细橙皮屑和烤杏仁片的光泽。汉娜屏住呼吸，看着格雷厄姆拿起一把干净的叉子。接下来会发生什么？请先完整听一遍这一幕。
Here goes Judge Graham with forkful number one — nobody say a word!
Notice how the fork glides straight through without a hammer or safety goggles.
Wait... let a man chew properly before you two start celebrating.
He took a second bite! Tessa, he did not make the brass polish face!
Well, Graham? Tell us honestly — is that worthy of our Saturday anniversary table?
Hand me my paper notebook and my carpenter pencil from beside the teapot, Hannah.
He is writing in capital letters... TEN OUT OF TEN, DO NOT CHANGE A THING!
YES! Ten out of ten in Graham's pencil is worth three gold medals!
Purely for structural safety, however, I should test one more small corner slice.
Aha! Caught you asking for seconds, Mister Tough Judge!
Eat all you want, Graham, and write down four full cakes for Saturday!
Keep baking like this, Tessa, and half of Portland will line up outside our gate.
现在让我们逐句品味这个万众期待的裁决时刻吧。
Here goes Judge Graham with forkful number one — nobody say a word!
“格雷厄姆裁判要吃第一叉了——谁都别出声！”汉娜像体育解说员一样播报着这一刻：
Here goes Judge Graham
Here goes 常用来宣布某件事即将开始，并且主语要放在动词 goes 后面（Here goes Judge Graham）。
forkful number one
后缀 -ful 表示“……所能容纳的量”：比如 forkful（一叉子的量）、spoonful（一勺的量）、handful（一把的量）。
Notice how the fork glides straight through without a hammer or safety goggles.
“你看叉子直接顺滑地切进去了，根本不用锤子也不需要安全护目镜。”泰莎带着调侃夸赞起自己的新作品：
Notice how the fork glides straight through
notice 的意思是“注意到、留意”，别和表示“新闻、消息”的 news 搞混了。glide 形容动作轻柔顺滑、毫不费力。
safety goggles.
goggles 指全包式的护目镜或泳镜，而日常戴的普通眼镜是 glasses。
Wait... let a man chew properly before you two start celebrating.
“等等……在你们俩开始庆祝之前，先让人好好嚼一嚼。”格雷厄姆依旧一本正经地请大家耐心等他吃完：
let a man chew properly
chew（咀嚼）开头的 ch 发 /tʃ/ 音；properly（好好地、恰当地）派生自形容词 proper。
before you two start celebrating.
因为 you 既可以指“你”也可以指“你们”，口语里常用 you two 来明确指“你们俩”；start 后面既可以接 -ing 也可以接 to + 动词原形。
He took a second bite! Tessa, he did not make the brass polish face!
“他又咬了第二口！泰莎，他没有露出像舔了擦铜膏一样的表情！”汉娜紧盯着裁判的每一个微表情欢呼起来：
He took a second bite!
英语里说“咬一口”最自然的搭配是 take a bite，这里的 took 是 take 的不规则过去式。
he did not make the brass polish face!
make a face 意思是“做鬼脸、露出怪表情”；前面用了助动词 did not 后，动词要恢复原形 make。
Well, Graham? Tell us honestly — is that worthy of our Saturday anniversary table?
“怎么样，格雷厄姆？老实告诉我们——这配得上我们周六的周年庆餐桌吗？”泰莎再也按捺不住心中的悬念：
Tell us honestly
honestly 词首的 h 不发音，和 hour 一样，读作 /ˈɑːnəstli/。
worthy of our Saturday anniversary table?
worthy of 相当于“配得上、值得”；英语里星期几的名称首字母永远要大写。
Hand me my paper notebook and my carpenter pencil from beside the teapot, Hannah.
“汉娜，把茶壶旁边我的纸质笔记本和木工铅笔递给我。”格雷厄姆准备把评语白纸黑字写下来：
Hand me my paper notebook
hand 除了表示“手”之外，还可以直接用作动词，意思是“顺手递给某人某物”。
from beside the teapot,
英语允许两个介词连用，例如这里的 from beside，意思是“从……旁边”。
He is writing in capital letters... TEN OUT OF TEN, DO NOT CHANGE A THING!
“他正在用全大写字母写……十分满分，什么都别改！”汉娜凑在格雷厄姆肩头念出了结果：
in capital letters...
capital letters 指“大写字母”，而“小写字母”则是 lowercase letters。
TEN OUT OF TEN,
打分时用 out of（ten out of ten）。而 do not change a thing 是一种很有力的强调说法，意思是“一点儿也别改”。
YES! Ten out of ten in Graham's pencil is worth three gold medals!
“太棒了！格雷厄姆用铅笔写下的十分满分，抵得上三枚金牌！”泰莎高兴得欢呼起来：
in Graham's pencil
在人名后面加 's 表示所有格，如 Graham's pencil（格雷厄姆的铅笔），拥有者放在前面。
is worth three gold medals!
注意 worth 是形容词或介词，不是动词，所以表达“值……”时要说 be worth，句子里必须加上系动词 is。
Purely for structural safety, however, I should test one more small corner slice.
“不过，纯出于结构安全考虑，我得再尝一小块边角的蛋糕。”格雷厄姆用严谨的工程术语掩饰自己还想再吃一口的馋意：
Purely for structural safety,
purely 来自 pure（纯粹的），意思是“纯粹地、仅仅”。
however,
however 前后加上逗号时，可以插在句中；I should test 表示“我应当测试一下”。
Aha! Caught you asking for seconds, Mister Tough Judge!
“抓到你要再来一块了吧，铁面大裁判先生！”汉娜当场拆穿了他；口语中常像这样省略开头的 I（I caught you）：
Caught you asking for seconds,
catch someone doing something 意思是“当场抓到某人做某事”；这里的 seconds 指餐厅或吃甜点时“再来一份、第二份”。
Mister Tough Judge!
tough 意思是“严厉的、苛刻的”；结尾的 gh 发 /f/ 的音，读作 /tʌf/。
Eat all you want, Graham, and write down four full cakes for Saturday!
“格雷厄姆，你想吃多少就吃多少，顺便记下来星期六要做四个整蛋糕！”泰莎已经开始筹划周年庆当天的烘焙量了：
Eat all you want,
all you want 中间省略了关系代词 that，和中文“你想吃多少就吃多少”一样自然顺口。
write down four full cakes
短语动词 write down 意思是“写下来、记下”。
Keep baking like this, Tessa, and half of Portland will line up outside our gate.
“泰莎，照这样烤下去，半个波特兰的人都要在咱们大门外排起长队了。”格雷厄姆用他特有的方式给出了最高赞美：
Keep baking like this,
keep 后面接动词的 -ing 形式表示“持续不断地做某事”。
will line up outside our gate.
line up 在美式英语中是“排队”，而在英式英语里通常会说 queue up。下面请再从头到尾听一遍完整的对话。
Here goes Judge Graham with forkful number one — nobody say a word!
Notice how the fork glides straight through without a hammer or safety goggles.
Wait... let a man chew properly before you two start celebrating.
He took a second bite! Tessa, he did not make the brass polish face!
Well, Graham? Tell us honestly — is that worthy of our Saturday anniversary table?
Hand me my paper notebook and my carpenter pencil from beside the teapot, Hannah.
He is writing in capital letters... TEN OUT OF TEN, DO NOT CHANGE A THING!
YES! Ten out of ten in Graham's pencil is worth three gold medals!
Purely for structural safety, however, I should test one more small corner slice.
Aha! Caught you asking for seconds, Mister Tough Judge!
Eat all you want, Graham, and write down four full cakes for Saturday!
Keep baking like this, Tessa, and half of Portland will line up outside our gate.
第三批蛋糕在格雷厄姆的纸质账本上拿下了历史性的十分满分——外加一份以“严格安全测试”为名的第二块蛋糕！回头见！
See you later!
